chapter_theme: A short song at Thiruvamur (headed திருவர்முர்): a voice sick with love says the burning of the cool moon, Kama's bow and the beating sea leave the night as long as an aeon, and turns to Kumaresa on the peacock, life of his loving devotees, who makes Death turn his back.

739.reading: A short love song: the speaker asks whether the night as long as an aeon must be spent this way, burned by the fire of the cool moon, by the bow Kama bends in anger and by the sea whose waves beat on. The song names Murugan as Kumaresa on the peacock at Thiruvamur, the great life of his loving devotees, who makes Death show his back.
739.nuance: The four torments (moon, Kama's bow, the sea, the endless night) are the stock signs of a woman's love-sickness in akam poetry; the song has no confession of sin, so the speaker is the lover longing for Murugan, though the text does not name her. காலன் முதுகை விரிக்கும், making Death turn his back in flight, sets the Lord against Death even in a love song. படியொதான் is probably படியோதான். மாது புகழை வளர்க்கும் may allude to a woman of the shrine's story, which I cannot identify.

links.note: In 739 the lover asks whether the night as long as an aeon (ஊழி இரவு) must be spent burned by the moon, Kama's bow and the beating sea. Kural 1169 says these long nights (நெடிய கழியும் இரா) are crueller than the cruel man himself. Both make the lengthened night the separated lover's torment; the song addresses it to Murugan.

source_issues: Heading and song 739 line 5: திருவர்முர் is probably a corruption of திருவாமூர் (Thiruvamur).
Song 739 line 4: படியொதான் is probably படியோதான்.
